searchText: FYI: proposal for a mev-boost circuit breaker to go into CLs ASAP https://hackmd.io/@ralexstokes/BJn9N6Thc is there a specific attack this is supposed to defend against? It seems reasonable, not not particularly difficult to implement, but https://hackmd.io/@ralexstokes/BJn9N6Thc#recovery-condition seems like it would eventually trigger on all but the most solid networks. https://sepolia.beaconcha.in/ shows three missing blocks in a row frequently and four semi-regularly (at least a couple of times in the last few hours). that seems pretty close to the threshold of five It's not clear if those are just reorgs though, which are covered by the proposal the final number could be higher but to answer your question, this is a mitigation against the scenario where the builder network fails to release blocks when they should Isn't that what the 1 second timeout before using backup EL block construction is for? if there is a buggy or malicious relay, then they could fail to release the execution payload needed to form the full block in this setting the proposer has already signed the commitment oh, that would be a problem, yes that timeout is in the event of a slow relay, more than a failing or even malicious relay hopefully we never need this breaker to trigger, but it would be good to have an absolute fail safe sure, agree hey <@199561711278227457> (mev-boost @ Flashbots, here). Trying to scope testing expectations for goerli shadow forks ahead of prater merge, can <@268793214906007562> and I dm? Sent a friend request, was blocked from sending. Ahhh, sorry about that. Just sent you both a request.
